claims.claim_text: Air Products' NEOM Green Hydrogen Company joint venture closed $6.1 billion non-recourse financing in May 2023 for the world's largest green hydrogen-based ammonia production facility, and APD is the primary beneficiary that consolidates the VIE.
claims.source_quote: in May, our NEOM Green Hydrogen Company joint venture completed financial close on the world s largest green hydrogen-based ammonia production facility, securing $6.1 billion of non-recourse financing from local, regional, and international banks and financial institutions ... We are the primary beneficiary of the NEOM Green Hydrogen Company and consolidate the joint venture within our Middle East and India segment.
claims.subject: NEOM Green Hydrogen Company
claims.extraction_notes: External validation: count SEC filings referencing the named JV before cutoff. A NEOM JV of this size with $6.1B project finance should generate multiple filer references across the period; absence would be a red flag.

claims.claim_text: Air Products issued performance guarantees of up to approximately $1.2 billion as EPC contractor for the NEOM Green Hydrogen Project, with exposure expiring November 2028.
claims.source_quote: We issued performance guarantees as a condition of project financing associated with the NEOM Green Hydrogen Project that would require us to pay up to approximately $1.2 billion in the event of nonperformance in our role as EPC contractor. Our exposure will decline over time before expiring in November 2028.
claims.subject: Air Products and Chemicals, Inc.
claims.extraction_notes: Verify APD's own subsequent filings (10-Qs filed after the 10-K but before cutoff) continue to disclose the NEOM performance guarantee at consistent magnitude. Material commitments of this size should recur in every quarterly filing.

claims.claim_text: Air Products operates approximately 450 production and distribution facilities in the Americas segment, including pipeline systems in the U.S. Gulf Coast, California, and Arizona.
claims.source_quote: Our Americas segment operates from approximately 450 production and distribution facilities in North and South America. Of these facilities, approximately 25% are located on owned property. We have sufficient property rights and permits for the ongoing operation of our pipeline systems in the Gulf Coast, California, and Arizona in the United States and Alberta and Ontario in Canada.
claims.subject: Air Products Americas segment
claims.extraction_notes: Test Texas (Gulf Coast hub) as representative anchor of the Americas footprint. EPA FRS should show numerous Air Products facilities in TX matching pipeline/production claim. Connector requires single-state param; additional state checks (CA, AZ, LA) would corroborate.

claims.claim_text: Air Products and its joint venture (with JIGPC) supply industrial gases to Saudi Aramco under a long-term sale-of-equipment contract tied to the Jazan gasification and power project.
claims.source_quote: long-term sale of equipment contract with the JIGPC joint venture to engineer, procure, and construct the industrial gas facilities that will supply gases to Aramco. We provided bank guarantees to the joint venture to support our performance under the contract.
claims.subject: Saudi Aramco
claims.extraction_notes: Aramco is a foreign filer (limited SEC presence) so direct counterparty-CIK check is impractical; instead test that the Jazan project name appears across multiple SEC filings — broad external corroboration of project existence.

claims.claim_text: Air Products has approximately $15 billion of committed capital to low- and zero-carbon hydrogen and other 'first mover' energy-transition projects, including clean-hydrogen and SAF projects in California, Louisiana, and Alberta.
claims.source_quote: As of the end of fiscal year 2023, we have committed capital of approximately $15 billion to projects intended to accelerate the energy transition ... We expect capital expenditures for fiscal year 2024 to be approximately $5.0 billion to $5.5 billion, which is driven by clean hydrogen and sustainable aviation fuel projects such as those being executed in California and Louisiana, United States, as well as Alberta, Canada.
claims.subject: Air Products and Chemicals, Inc.
claims.extraction_notes: Louisiana blue-hydrogen project: an EPA-regulated industrial facility should already be registered with FRS during permitting/construction. Presence of an APD-named site in LA supports the project moving past announcement; absence is a 'planned vs operational' red flag (Calibration Heuristic 3).

claims.claim_text: In March 2023 Air Products issued its inaugural multi-currency green bonds in concurrent USD and EUR fixed-rate note offerings with aggregate principal of $600 million and EUR 700 million, becoming the first U.S. chemical company to qualify green and blue hydrogen as eligible green-bond expenditure.
claims.source_quote: In March, we issued our inaugural green bonds in concurrent $600 and 700 million debt offerings, making Air Products the first U.S. chemical company to qualify green and blue hydrogen projects as an eligible expenditure category.
claims.subject: Air Products and Chemicals, Inc.
claims.extraction_notes: Bond issuance generates prospectus supplement (424B), free-writing prospectus (FWP), and pricing 8-K filings on EDGAR. Verify the March 2023 window contains the expected filings.

claims.claim_text: Air Products reports approximately 23,000 employees globally and ~$12.6 billion of fiscal-2023 sales with no single customer accounting for more than 10% of consolidated sales.
claims.source_quote: Approximately 23,000 passionate, talented, and committed employees ... Sales of $12.6 billion ... No single customer accounts for more than 10% of our consolidated sales.
claims.subject: Air Products and Chemicals, Inc.
claims.extraction_notes: Headcount, revenue, and 'no >10% customer' assertions are internal accounting figures. No external registry adjudicates total revenue or employee count for a global multinational. Audited financials are the canonical source; this claim is structurally not adjudicatable by an external M-source.
